comments.selected: Draft for the EBS pollock assessment and ESP teams. This contribution expands the EBS pollock ESP framework in the September 2026 assessment development document. It combines the pollock bibliography, the recruitment causal review, primary papers, and the assessment website. The present contribution establishes the scientific synthesis, incorporates annual age-0 energy density through 2025, and documents the existing indicator-analysis pilot. Recorded working indicator series and economic observations are included below. This contribution is Appendix B of the SAFE. The main finding is that fall age-0 energetic condition and juvenile exposure to predators provide strong biological reasons for organizing the ESP around successive survival stages. Physical indicators help describe those processes. The temperature and cold-pool fits remain research results; designation as predictive indicators requires additional numerical and prediction checks.

The source describes annual means. Sampling season, exact regional boundaries, annual weighting, sample sizes, measurement consistency, and uncertainty require contributor confirmation. These definitions will determine whether the observations represent pre-winter condition and which region matches the recruitment response. Energy density measures energy per unit dry mass. Estimating total energy per fish requires compatible individual dry mass and aggregation methods. Regional means remain separate, and 2026 energy-density observations are pending.

The 2026 NOAA temperature page reports an EBS survey domain, whereas the 2025 survey included both eastern and northern Bering Sea areas (Alaska Fisheries Science Center 2026a). Comparisons of area occupied, centers of distribution, temperature exposure, and predator overlap should therefore use a common domain or explicitly describe differences in coverage.
Total energy in kJ per fish additionally depends on fish dry mass and appropriate individual-level aggregation.
Translation into an age-1 forecasting component requires testing the corresponding response and lag.
Predator abundance, spatial overlap, diet, biomass consumed, and predation mortality describe successive parts of this process and require separate definitions.
The pilot’s same-year cold-pool edge is retained as a research proxy, with this timing question identified for review.

Adult Productivity and Observation Processes Adult growth, condition, maturity, distribution, and consumption connect recruitment to biomass production and future spawning output. Weight at age and condition should retain age, sex where available, season, gear, and location. Survey distribution indices also help evaluate changing availability to sampling. Changes in survey footprint or in the transformation of observations into annual estimates require documented comparison before they become evidence of a biological change.

comments.selected: The proposed workflow defines the response and cohort timing, assembles the literature-based mechanism table, draws a conceptual graph, and selects a small set of competing hypotheses. Statistical comparisons then use a common observation block and reference model. DSEM can organize these hypotheses while accounting for temporal dynamics (Thorson et al. 2024). Forecast evaluation and management strategy evaluation address whether environmentally informed recruitment methods improve decisions under uncertainty (Haltuch et al. 2019). The competing hypotheses from the recruitment review are: prey and age-0 energy; predator overlap; spawning and transport; and interactions between prey limitation and predator exposure over time. The present pilot fits only two direct proxy edges. Expansion should prioritize measured intermediates while retaining a small set of graphs that can be identified from the available series. Proposed Energy-Density Pathway The new observations allow a measured-condition hypothesis alongside the SST and cold-pool proxies: prey and thermal conditions in birth year t affect age-0 energy density, which contributes to overwinter survival and age-1 recruitment in t+1. This is a candidate pathway derived from the literature and workshop synthesis (Heintz et al. 2013; Siddon et al. 2013; Monnahan et al. 2026). It advances the age-1 focus described in the ESR coordination email (Siddon 2026). Confirm sampling season, response date, and regional overlap before assigning the observation to a pre-winter state. Evaluate SEBS and NBS individually before considering a combined regional index. Any regional aggregation requires documented weights and spatial coverage. The limited and different coverage supports a small set of competing pathways on a common observation block, with observation error and missing years handled explicitly. Preserve direct effects and intermediate-condition hypotheses as alternatives, and use withheld cohorts to evaluate prediction. The added data have descriptive and candidate explanatory roles in this revision; the expanded DSEM remains to be fitted. Existing DSEM Pilot

comments.selected: The working paper retains its fitted-state and forecast comparisons in the separate report. Its Figures 5–7 show IID, AR1 and recruitment- path state reconstructions. This appendix presents the observed input histories. Numerical and Scientific Validation The live CSV files label all four fits OK and record positive-definite Hessians. Recalculation of the diagnostic gate shows that the SST-only fit’s maximum gradient, 1.52×10 − 4, exceeds the required 10 − 4. The other three pass that gradient threshold. Tightening and rechecking the SST-only fit is required before treating its numerical estimates as a finalized comparison. Compilation and warning logs were outside the archived CSV evidence reviewed here and require confirmation with the fit archive. The remaining scientific checks are cohort and seasonal timing, alternative spatial domains, observation-error sensitivity, retrospective stability, residual patterns, competing mechanisms, and terminal-year or blocked prediction. Forecast tests must use the assessment estimate and environmental information available at each historical prediction date; later assessment revisions can otherwise introduce future information. Report both uncertainty calibration and improvement over the reference model. A common data block is required within each comparison, with shorter biological series evaluated on their explicitly defined subset.

comments.selected: Evidence The working indicator inventory, descriptive time series and economic context support the annual synthesis within their stated source limits. Primary indicator metadata remain incomplete. The standalone working paper retains its own inputs, uncertainty assumptions and forecast evaluation. An updated fish-oil yield series, in tons of oil per 100 tons of retained catch, requires oil-specific production and matching retained-catch totals for shoreside and at-sea processing. The grouped production sources combine oil with other products, while the older oil-specific records end in 2021 and lack processing mode. Mode-specific oil yields therefore remain unavailable.
The recorded working series add a mixed 2026 physical and prey context, while their metadata and biological interpretation remain subject to source and contributor checks.

The standalone DSEM’s terminal age-1 states are conditional estimates for missing years, and AR1 has lower RMSE in the recorded forecast comparison. Predictive use therefore requires further evaluation against that benchmark.
